cards.title: Second baby brings forgotten parenting challenges
cards.body: A parent shares how having a second child has made her realize how much she's forgotten about baby care, from feeding to teething. Her mother's help has been invaluable, while also stirring up memories of her own carefree childhood.

cards.title: Should AI technology replace parental judgment?
cards.body: Tech companies offer parents eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts, and optimized nap predictions. The article questions whether parents actually need these tools or if they create unnecessary anxiety.

cards.title: Empty nest emotions: when children leave home
cards.body: A parent explores the surprising emotional pain of seeing her first son prepare for university, challenging the assumption that 'empty nesting' is simply nature taking its course. Letters from other parents echo this complex grieving process.

cards.title: Is parental power bad for children?
cards.body: This article examines whether using parental authority is inherently disrespectful to children or can be exercised appropriately. It explores the balance between guidance and respecting a child's autonomy.

cards.title: Four discipline options when children break rules
cards.body: Parents have multiple approaches when responding to rule-breaking behavior. This article outlines key disciplinary options available to families.

cards.title: Lessons from being a second-time mom
cards.body: Six weeks into parenting two children, a mother reflects on surprising challenges and lessons the second time around. Her experience reveals that no two pregnancies or children are the same.

cards.title: Five breastfeeding findings every parent needs
cards.body: Breastfeeding research continues to evolve with new insights for new and expecting parents. This article highlights five important findings that can inform parenting decisions.

cards.title: Setting financial boundaries with adult children
cards.body: Parents often struggle to enforce financial limits with grown children. Replacing 'I can't afford it' with firmer language helps establish genuine boundaries.

cards.title: Emotional regulation prevents harm in children
cards.body: Teaching children to tolerate difficult feelings is key to preventing aggression, addiction, and violence. Emotional regulation should be treated as essential, not just a soft skill.

cards.title: Runny eggs pose salmonella risk for young children
cards.body: Health officials warn pregnant women, under-fives, over-65s, and immunocompromised individuals to avoid runny eggs when eating out. The guidance follows a reported salmonella outbreak.

cards.title: Child stars and addiction: pressures of early fame
cards.body: Experts warn that childhood stardom creates unusually high substance abuse risks for young actors. Intense pressure, drug access, and isolation contribute to addiction vulnerability.

cards.title: Postpartum psychosis and criminal responsibility examined
cards.body: A court hears testimony about command hallucinations associated with postpartum psychosis in a case involving a mother accused of harming her children. The case highlights severe mental health crises affecting new parents.
